coordinate_policy: Public LiDAR acquisition geography only; never protected archaeological-site coordinates or community-controlled locations. Study metadata is separate from map geometry. Each footprint is labeled as released GIS, digitized from a published map, reconstructed from published evidence, or contextual only. A ground footprint is not a literal aircraft GNSS trajectory.

surveys.name: UAV-LiDAR prototype tests
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: The prototype test area was evaluated for archaeological remote sensing, but no publishable acquisition footprint is mapped.
surveys.footprint_note: Generalized test landscape; not an exact flight footprint.
surveys.description: Generalized eastern Acre test landscape for the platform that preceded dedicated archaeological LiDAR surveys.
surveys.resolution_basis: The 2017 paper documents the UAV-LiDAR platform, but does not publish a terrain-raster cell size or a public terrain product for this test area.

surveys.name: Mound-village LiDAR transects
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: The published archaeological study analyzed all three mapped acquisition transects.
surveys.footprint_note: Three acquisition polygons digitized from Figure 2 against its published graticule and normalized to the reported 65.61 km² total; no flight-centerline file was released.
surveys.description: Generalized southeastern Acre study region for the Dona Maria, Estrela do Norte, and Dois Círculos transects.
surveys.resolution_basis: The open paper documents its flight and processing workflow but does not report the exported DEM cell size; no public raster or LAS/LAZ deposit was identified.

surveys.name: EBA–Sustainable Landscapes released transects
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: Peripato et al. screened 861 lines drawn from EBA, MSA, and TREES, but no public crosswalk identifies which of these 1,002 EBA polygon parts were included.
surveys.region: 901 distributed transect records across the Brazilian Amazon
surveys.footprint_note: The public L3A shapefile releases 901 acquisition records, represented by 1,002 polygon parts, from the 2016 and 2017–2018 campaigns. They are ground-coverage boundaries, not aircraft GPS trajectories, and should not be conflated one-for-one with the 861 transects screened by Peripato et al.
metrics: Public vector footprints and point-cloud archive
surveys.description: The public EBA archive exposes the actual distributed acquisition footprints behind a large part of Brazil’s ecological LiDAR coverage. Some of these data were later repurposed for archaeology, but the archive itself is not an archaeological screen.
surveys.resolution_basis: The EBA campaign methods document classification of ground returns and interpolation of each transect into a 1 m digital terrain model. The public release provides point clouds and acquisition footprints; the nominal density of about 4 returns/m² is a separate acquisition measure.

surveys.name: Forest-covered geoglyph samples

surveys.footprint_note: Broad context only; the publication altered example coordinates.
surveys.description: Broad eastern Acre context for two protected example tiles. The publication altered their coordinates, so this is not a footprint.
surveys.resolution_basis: The study used published 1 m terrain models.

surveys.name: Casarabe low-density urbanism survey
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: All six mapped acquisition areas were analyzed for archaeological landscape features.
surveys.footprint_note: Six separate scan blocks digitized against the UTM grid and normalized together to the published 204 km² total; the regional envelope was not scanned continuously.
surveys.description: Airborne LiDAR documented monumental centers, smaller settlements, causeways, canals, and reservoirs.
surveys.resolution_basis: The paper reports 0.5 m/pixel DEMs, generally 18 million raw points/km².

surveys.name: Upano Valley urban network
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: The study reports intensive analysis of 300 km² within the 600 km² acquisition.
surveys.footprint_note: Irregular acquisition boundary reconstructed from the published regional map and normalized to the reported 600 km²; it is not an aircraft trajectory.
surveys.description: In the forested Upper Amazon drainage at the eastern foot of the Andes, LiDAR exposed a connected landscape of platforms, plazas, roads, drainage works, and agricultural terraces.
surveys.resolution_basis: The supplementary methods report a preprocessed 1 m DEM.

surveys.name: ONF French Guiana acquisition archive
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: Selected acquisitions have archaeological studies, but no comprehensive review of all 79 polygon parts is published.
surveys.region: Public ONF acquisition extents across French Guiana
surveys.footprint_note: The public WFS exposes 66 acquisition records represented by 79 polygon parts. These are released ground-coverage boundaries, not flight-centerline trajectories.
surveys.description: A public forestry LiDAR acquisition archive with potential archaeological reuse. The atlas maps only released acquisition polygons and does not imply that every polygon has been archaeologically screened.
surveys.resolution_basis: The public acquisition synthesis supplies geometry and campaign metadata, but not one comparable terrain-grid resolution for every polygon.

surveys.name: Saül–Mont Galbao forest survey
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: Project reporting identifies about a dozen sites in more than 15,000 ha without documenting a complete archaeological screen.
surveys.footprint_note: Generalized named-area envelope rather than exact acquisition boundaries.
metrics: About a dozen ring-ditch or crowned-mountain sites
surveys.description: Public project reporting describes airborne LiDAR detection of hilltop and ring-ditch features under forest.
surveys.resolution_basis: The park reports metric-precision surface, terrain, and height models, but does not state their raster cell size; positional precision is not treated as pixel resolution.

surveys.name: Nouragues crowned-mountain study
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: The study interpreted LiDAR terrain models at its three named archaeological sites.
surveys.footprint_note: Two released ONF acquisition extents contain MC87 and Nouragues. The paper credits separate PAG LiDAR for Mont Galbao, but no public acquisition boundary was identified.
metrics: 2 sites matched to released ONF acquisition GIS
Mont Galbao boundary not publicly resolved
surveys.description: Research combined LiDAR-derived terrain evidence with archaeological interpretation of modified hilltops.
surveys.resolution_basis: Published mapping of the 2012 Nouragues ALS uses a 1 m raster DEM.

surveys.name: Río Abiseo–Gran Pajatén survey
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: The mapped acquisition was analyzed as an archaeological documentation survey.
surveys.region: Río Abiseo National Park, San Martín
surveys.footprint_note: Unfilled park-scale context. The reported airborne scan covered about 4,000 ha, not the entire park outline.
metrics: >100 structures documented through later integrated work
surveys.description: Airborne LiDAR and later close-range and field mapping expanded documentation of the Gran Pajatén landscape.
surveys.resolution_basis: The public project sources describe the airborne scan and resulting 3D terrain model but do not publish its cell size or point density.

surveys.name: Kuélap drone-LiDAR documentation
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: The mapped acquisition was analyzed as an archaeological documentation survey.
surveys.footprint_note: Site-scale envelope aligned to Peru's public IDEP Kuélap drone-imagery layer; the exact 2020 LiDAR flight boundary is not released.
metrics: Known monumental stone complex documented—not a new regional discovery
surveys.description: A site-scale project documented Kuélap’s monumental walls, hundreds of circular structures, and terrain rather than surveying a broad lowland landscape.
surveys.resolution_basis: The paper reports approximately 2,000 points/m² but describes bare-earth model resolution as variable, so no DTM cell size is assigned.

surveys.name: Madre de Dios ecological ALS archive
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: No published archaeological screen of this exact ecological ALS archive was found in English or Spanish searches.
surveys.footprint_note: Thirteen documented 2009 CAO blocks are digitized from Marvin et al. 2013 Figure 1 and normalized individually to the per-block areas in Table 1 (1,254.21 km² when its rows are summed). They are a published subset of the broader 27-area archive.
metrics: 514,317 ha of actual ALS in 27 separate areas
0 published archaeological screens or ancient-work detections
surveys.description: A forest-carbon sampling archive, not a wall-to-wall scan. No archaeological screening or ancient structures from these 27 samples have been published, and the raw point cloud was not deposited with the paper.
surveys.resolution_basis: The primary study reports LiDAR acquisition at 1 m spatial resolution or finer across its 27 survey areas.

surveys.name: Colombian forest-carbon ALS archive
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: No published archaeological screen of this exact forest-carbon archive was found in English or Spanish searches.
surveys.footprint_note: Thirty-two unobscured flight blocks are digitized from the published overview and width-normalized proportionally to the reported 465,622 ha total. Six of the 38 blocks cannot be resolved independently.
surveys.description: Airborne LiDAR collected for forest carbon. It is mapped as research potential, not as evidence that earthworks were found.
surveys.resolution_basis: The primary paper reports 1.12 m laser-spot spacing and about two returns per spot (approximately 1.6 returns/m²), but no archaeological terrain-grid cell size.

surveys.name: Guyana national LiDAR base mapping
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: No published archaeological review was found, and the available mapping is not treated as archaeology-usable coverage.
surveys.source_label: Guyana Lands and Surveys Commission / FAO
surveys.footprint_note: Country-scale program geography; the public notice does not provide exact target polygons.
surveys.description: A government base-mapping campaign with potential terrain data for archaeology, but no confirmed archaeological analysis.
surveys.resolution_basis: The FAO procurement specifies 2 points/m² in rural areas and 10 points/m² in urban areas, but the delivered terrain-grid cell size is not public. The stored density is the rural specification.

surveys.name: Kuikuro community-led drone LiDAR

surveys.footprint_note: Community-controlled project geography; exact villages, excavations, and data are not mapped.
surveys.description: Collaborative Kuikuro research uses drone LiDAR at site scale. Only a broad Upper Xingu context is shown.
surveys.resolution_basis: The Science report describes community-controlled drone LiDAR; it publishes neither a terrain-grid cell size nor an open data product.

surveys.name: La Lindosa terrestrial 3D documentation
surveys.archaeology_review_scope: The documented rock-art panels were analyzed archaeologically, but this is terrestrial recording rather than mapped airborne coverage.
